## Overview

Replace the human-readable body of every wiki doc page with a **System One typed-decision record** — a uniform `{ state, questions, answers }` envelope whose questions are **type-appropriate** (`choice` / `score` / `noul`). The records become the **canonical doc format**, the **training corpus** for WM's own small local decision model, and the **runtime input** the model answers over. Human readability is explicitly **not** a requirement.

Built on the feasibility spike `@doc/specs/system-one-model-application` (report `@doc/concepts/system-one-feasibility`), which established that the local path is a thin custom `ort` wrapper around a sub-200M ONNX decision model.

## Locked Decisions

- **D-A**: The typed record **replaces the page body** (not an add-on).
- **D-B**: A **uniform envelope** for every page — `{ state, questions, answers }` — with **per-page-type question sets**.
- **D-C**: The records are simultaneously the **canonical format**, the **training corpus**, and the **runtime input**.
- **D-D**: Keep the existing YAML **frontmatter** (`id`/`title`/`type`/`status`/`tags`/`relates_to`); the **body is a strict machine record**. Human readability is **not required**.
- **D-E**: **One-shot conversion** of all existing doc pages (~193: 35 decision, 17 rule, 58 pattern, 65 concept, 12 howto, 6 reference).

## Record Envelope

```yaml
state: <the page's source situation as text or structured JSON>
questions:
  - id: <stable question id>
    type: choice          # choice | score | noul
    instructions: <what is being decided>
    options: [<label>, ...]   # choice only, >= 2
  - id: <id>
    type: score
    instructions: <...>
    levels: [<label>, ...]    # score only, 2..10, ordered
  - id: <id>
    type: noul
    instructions: <boolean condition>
answers:
  <question id>: <label | level index | true/false | probability>
```

### Per-type question sets (initial)

| Page type | Illustrative questions |
|---|---|
| decision | `chosen_option` (choice over considered options), `reversibility` (noul), `confidence` (score), `status` (choice) |
| rule | `applies_to` (choice), `enforcement` (choice), `severity` (score), `has_exception` (noul) |
| pattern | `problem_kind` (choice), `when_to_use` (noul), `complexity` (score) |
| concept | `category` (choice), `related_to` (choice, multi), `maturity` (score) |
| howto | `task_kind` (choice), `prerequisites_present` (noul), `difficulty` (score) |
| reference | `kind` (choice), `surface` (choice), `stability` (score) |

## Requirements

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-1**: Define the record envelope (`state`, `questions[]`, `answers`) as the canonical page body, with the question primitives `choice` / `score` / `noul`.
- **FR-2**: Preserve YAML frontmatter unchanged (`id` double-quoted, `title`, `type`, `status`, `tags`, `relates_to`).
- **FR-3**: Define a per-page-type question schema for decision, rule, pattern, concept, howto, and reference.
- **FR-4**: The engine MUST parse the record body, expose it through a typed accessor (page read), and **round-trip it without corruption** using line-based editing helpers (never whole-block YAML round-trip).
- **FR-5**: `wm_validate` MUST reject malformed records: missing `state`; a question missing `id`/`type`/`instructions`; `choice` with < 2 options; `score` outside 2–10 levels; an answer whose key is not a question id, or whose value is invalid for the question type.
- **FR-6**: Provide a **one-shot migration** converting all existing doc pages to the format, preserving frontmatter and page id, and reporting any page it cannot convert.
- **FR-7**: Emit a **training corpus** as JSONL rows `{"state", "questions", "answers"}` generated from the records.
- **FR-8**: Provide a **runtime path** where a local decision model answers the questions for a given `state` — reusing the custom-`ort` sub-200M model path from the feasibility spec.
- **FR-9**: Migration MUST be **idempotent** — re-running it on already-converted pages is a no-op.

### Non-Functional Requirements

- **NFR-1**: Machine-first; human readability is not a requirement (body may be strict data).
- **NFR-2**: Round-trip safety — never whole-block YAML round-trip; always double-quote `id`; use the existing line-based frontmatter helpers.
- **NFR-3**: No data loss — every converted page retains its id/title/type/status/tags/relates_to byte-for-byte.
- **NFR-4**: Fully local and offline; no hosted API (per `@doc/specs/system-one-model-application` D5).
- **NFR-5**: Validation is deterministic and covered by tests.
- **NFR-6**: Existing search/graph/task behaviour must not regress.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: The envelope and all six per-type question sets are documented with exact field specs.
- [ ] AC-2: All ~193 target pages are converted; **0 pages** fail to parse; the migration reports a per-type conversion count.
- [ ] AC-3: `wm_validate` catches each malformed-record case in FR-5, proven by tests.
- [ ] AC-4: A round-trip test (parse → write → parse) yields identical records and identical frontmatter.
- [ ] AC-5: A JSONL training corpus is emitted with one row per page and valid `state`/`questions`/`answers`.
- [ ] AC-6: A runtime query answers the questions for a given state via the local model path (or the path is documented and stubbed if the model is not yet integrated).
- [ ] AC-7: No converted page loses or alters its frontmatter fields.
- [ ] AC-8: Re-running the migration leaves already-converted pages unchanged.
- [ ] AC-9: No regression in page read, graph edges, or search.

## Scenarios

### Scenario 1: Convert a decision page
**Given** a decision page with Context/Decision/Rationale/Consequences prose
**When** the migration runs
**Then** its body becomes a record whose `state` carries the context, `questions` include the chosen option and reversibility, `answers` record the actual decision, and frontmatter is untouched.

### Scenario 2: Reject a malformed record
**Given** a page whose body has a `choice` question with one option, or an answer key not matching any question
**When** `wm_validate` runs
**Then** it reports a deterministic error naming the page and field.

### Scenario 3: Training corpus export
**Given** all pages converted
**When** the export runs
**Then** it writes one JSONL row per page, each a valid record.

### Scenario 4: Runtime decision query
**Given** a new state and a page type's question set
**When** the runtime query runs
**Then** the local model returns typed answers with confidences, offline.

## Technical Notes

- Reuse the existing frontmatter parser and **line-based helpers** (`set_yaml_field` / `remove_yaml_block` / `ac_set_checked`); never whole-block YAML round-trip (see `@doc/patterns/line-based-frontmatter-editing`).
- The record body is YAML so the existing markdown+YAML toolchain can parse it; a schema version field should be considered for forward-compatibility.
- The existing **duplicated-frontmatter / escaped-newline bug** on some pages (see `@doc/tasks/core-pages-carry-duplicated-frontmatter-blocks-and-escaped-newlines`) must be handled or fixed by the migration.
- Runtime model candidates come from `@doc/concepts/system-one-feasibility`: Verdict-small (118M, int8 112 MiB) or Julia-1 (144M) via a custom `ort` wrapper; Laya is too heavy for the 8 GB target.
- Excludes `task` and `spec` page types (out of scope for this conversion).

## Open Questions

- [ ] Exact final question set per page type (the table above is illustrative).
- [ ] Which local model backs the runtime path — pending the edge-typing head-to-head from the feasibility spec.
- [ ] How the runtime is surfaced — a new `wm_*` tool, an extension of page read, or a CLI command?
- [ ] Is a record schema version field required from day one?
- [ ] Should the raw human prose be archived anywhere before replacement, or discarded?

```yaml
    levels: [<label>, ...]    # score only, 2..10, ordered
  - id: <id>
    type: noul
    instructions: <boolean condition>
answers:
  <question id>: <label | level index | true/false | probability>
```

### Per-type question sets (initial)

| Page type | Illustrative questions |
|---|---|
| decision | `chosen_option` (choice over considered options), `reversibility` (noul), `confidence` (score), `status` (choice) |
| rule | `applies_to` (choice), `enforcement` (choice), `severity` (score), `has_exception` (noul) |
| pattern | `problem_kind` (choice), `when_to_use` (noul), `complexity` (score) |
| concept | `category` (choice), `related_to` (choice, multi), `maturity` (score) |
| howto | `task_kind` (choice), `prerequisites_present` (noul), `difficulty` (score) |
| reference | `kind` (choice), `surface` (choice), `stability` (score) |

## Requirements

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-1**: Define the record envelope (`state`, `questions[]`, `answers`) as the canonical page body, with the question primitives `choice` / `score` / `noul`.
- **FR-2**: Preserve YAML frontmatter unchanged (`id` double-quoted, `title`, `type`, `status`, `tags`, `relates_to`).
- **FR-3**: Define a per-page-type question schema for decision, rule, pattern, concept, howto, and reference.
- **FR-4**: The engine MUST parse the record body, expose it through a typed accessor (page read), and **round-trip it without corruption** using line-based editing helpers (never whole-block YAML round-trip).
- **FR-5**: `wm_validate` MUST reject malformed records: missing `state`; a question missing `id`/`type`/`instructions`; `choice` with < 2 options; `score` outside 2–10 levels; an answer whose key is not a question id, or whose value is invalid for the question type.
- **FR-6**: Provide a **one-shot migration** converting all existing doc pages to the format, preserving frontmatter and page id, and reporting any page it cannot convert.
- **FR-7**: Map a record's `state` + `questions` into the **off-the-shelf model's wire format** so the runtime can query it (no training or corpus export).
- **FR-8**: Provide a **runtime path** where the off-the-shelf model answers the questions for a given `state` — reusing the custom-`ort` sub-200M model path from the feasibility spec.
- **FR-9**: Migration MUST be **idempotent** — re-running it on already-converted pages is a no-op.
- **FR-10**: WM MUST obtain the off-the-shelf model via a **checksum-pinned download** (version + checksum recorded in a manifest), reusing the existing ONNX model-download integrity path. The model is **never committed to the repository**.

### Non-Functional Requirements

- **NFR-1**: Machine-first; human readability is not a requirement (body may be strict data).
- **NFR-2**: Round-trip safety — never whole-block YAML round-trip; always double-quote `id`; use the existing line-based frontmatter helpers.
- **NFR-3**: No data loss — every converted page retains its id/title/type/status/tags/relates_to byte-for-byte.
- **NFR-4**: Fully local and offline at runtime; no hosted API and no training (per `@doc/specs/system-one-model-application` D5).
- **NFR-5**: Validation is deterministic and covered by tests.
- **NFR-6**: Existing search/graph/task behaviour must not regress.
- **NFR-7**: The model artifact is not stored in version control; only its manifest (version + checksum) is.

- [ ] AC-2: All ~193 target pages are converted; **0 pages** fail to parse; the migration reports a per-type conversion count.

- [ ] AC-7: No converted page loses or alters its frontmatter fields.

- [ ] AC-10: The model is fetched via a **checksum-pinned download** (manifest version + checksum), is **not** committed to the repo, and the default runtime path uses it without any training.

## Scenarios

### Scenario 1: Convert a decision page
**Given** a decision page with Context/Decision/Rationale/Consequences prose
**When** the migration runs
**Then** its body becomes a record whose `state` carries the context, `questions` include the chosen option and reversibility, `answers` record the actual decision, and frontmatter is untouched.

**When** `wm_validate` runs
**Then** it reports a deterministic error naming the page and field.

## Technical Notes

- Reuse the existing frontmatter parser and **line-based helpers** (`set_yaml_field` / `remove_yaml_block` / `ac_set_checked`); never whole-block YAML round-trip (see `@doc/patterns/line-based-frontmatter-editing`).
- The record body is YAML so the existing markdown+YAML toolchain can parse it; a schema version field should be considered for forward-compatibility.
- The existing **duplicated-frontmatter / escaped-newline bug** on some pages (see `@doc/tasks/core-pages-carry-duplicated-frontmatter-blocks-and-escaped-newlines`) must be handled or fixed by the migration.
- Runtime model candidates come from `@doc/concepts/system-one-feasibility`: Verdict-small (118M, int8 112 MiB) or Julia-1 (144M) via a custom `ort` wrapper; Laya is too heavy for the 8 GB target.
- **Model distribution**: downloaded on demand, pinned by version + checksum in a manifest, never committed; reuse the existing ONNX model-download integrity path (and re-enable verification per `WM-005`). The repo carries only the manifest, not the artifact.
- **No training path exists in this spec** — training, fine-tuning, and training-corpus export are explicitly excluded.
- Excludes `task` and `spec` page types (out of scope for this conversion).

## Overview

Replace the human-readable body of the **convertible** wiki doc pages with a **System One typed-decision record** — a uniform `{ schema_version, state, questions, answers }` envelope whose questions are **type-appropriate** (`choice` / `score` / `noul`). Records are the **canonical doc format** and the **runtime input** an off-the-shelf local model answers over (`gliner-rs`). **No training is in scope.** Human readability is not a requirement.

The normative schema contract lives in `@doc/reference/typed-decision-record-schema` (v1). Built on `@doc/specs/system-one-model-application`, `@doc/concepts/system-one-feasibility`, and `@doc/concepts/typed-decision-application-map`.

## Locked Decisions

- **D-A**: The typed record **replaces the page body** (not an add-on).
- **D-B**: A **uniform envelope** for every converted page, with **per-page-type question sets** (fixed vocabularies; see schema doc).
- **D-C**: Records are the **canonical format** and the **runtime input** only. **Training is out of scope.**
- **D-D**: Keep YAML **frontmatter** (`id`/`title`/`type`/`status`/`tags`/`relates_to`); the **body is a strict machine record**. Readability not required.
- **D-E (revised)**: Convert only `decision`, `pattern`, `concept`, `howto`, `reference` (~160 pages: 37/61/46/10/6). **One-shot**.
- **D-F (revised)**: Runtime is `gliner-rs` + `GLiNER2.5-small-v1` (Apache-2.0); `score`/`noul` are **emulated** over its choice head. No training.
- **D-G**: The model is a **checksum-pinned download** (manifest in `.wm/models.json`), never committed.
- **D-H (blast radius)**: **Excluded from conversion** — `rule` (binding instructions read at session start), `core` (project conventions/architecture), `memory` (recall content injected into context), `task`, `spec`, `index.md`, `note`, and the steering files (`WIKI-MEM.md`, `AGENTS.md`, shims, `.wm/AGENTS.md`).
